newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Give up ground to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Give up ground to U.S..

text.p: Australian bonds underperformed against U.S. debt as the market awaited developments there in the wake of Friday's massive sell-off in U.S. stocks, although they held their own versus other dollar bloc members.
The local market had outpaced the U.S. late last week after data showed wages growth under control but remained well above the low of around 25 basis points seen a few weeks ago.
Analysts at Hambros Bank believe moderate economic growth, excellent inflation propects and the possibility of a sixth easing suggest the Aussie market should continue to outperform.
"However, in an environment of rising U.S. yields in coming months as the growth pulse picks up and inflationary corncerns emerge, the Australian market may underperform," they said in a report.
U.S. Treasury yields eased slightly in Tokyo trading on Monday after the mixed finish in New York on Friday.

Spreads to Canada narrowed, which had also dragged it heels to the U.S. on Friday, while the negative spreads to New Zealand grew. N.Z. yields ended higher, although comments by the RBNZ that monetary policy conditions were too loose drew a muted response.
